questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 10 + 10 + 10 ?
questions.explain: Count the 10s: there are 3 of them, so this is 3 groups of 10, which is 3 × 10 = 30. Counting one group too few gives 2 × 10, which is 10 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 10 × 10 or 2 × 3. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Jun Hao works out 4049 + 1749 in columns. One column makes 18, so he writes 8 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Jun Hao works out 4049 + 1749 in columns. One column makes 18, so he writes 8 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 18 is the ones column: 9 + 9 = 18, and no other column reaches ten. 18 ones is 1 ten and 8 ones, so the 8 stays in the ones column - worth 8 - and the small 1 goes above the tens column - worth 10. The small 1 is worth 10. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stemText: Aisyah had some marbles. She gave away 653 of them, then bought 255 more. Now she has 2882. How many marbles did she have at first?

questions.explain: Taking the same number away from the top and the bottom changes the amount. 1012 is not 810. To simplify you DIVIDE both by the same number: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6, so 1012 = 56. Carrying the same habit on to the answer would change the amount a second time: 56 is as far as it goes, and taking anything more off the top or the bottom makes a different fraction, not a simpler one.

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is between 24 and 78?
questions.stemText: Which of these fractions is between 2/4 and 7/8?
questions.explain: Step 1: the two ends are not written in the same size of piece, so cut 24 into 8ths first: 2 × 2 = 4 and 4 × 2 = 8, so 24 is the same amount as 48. Step 2: now every fraction is in 8ths, so just count the tops - the answer has to be more than 4 of them and fewer than 7. That is 68. 24 and 78 are the two ends themselves, so neither of them is between them.

questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 12 cm long and 9 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 2 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 3 cm of edge before the notch and 5 cm after it, and the banner is still 7 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 + 5 + 9 + 12 + 9 = 46 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 4 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 4 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 2 cm down and 2 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 9) + 2 × 2 = 46 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
